inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL JSON guide uses JSON_TABLE to turn JSON collections into relational rows and JSON_QUERY to extract object or array fragments from JSON documents.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a catalog-payload audit. JSON_TABLE exposes item identifiers and JSON payloads, while JSON_QUERY extracts nested object and array fragments and JSON_TYPE classifies the extracted shapes; the source guide text, literals, and application context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Two fixed catalog payloads expand into rows; one has object and array fragments and the other has a missing object path that must return SQL NULL.
determinism_notes: The JSON array order and outer item ID order are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.

steps.sql: SELECT jt.item_id, JSON_QUERY(jt.attributes, '$.details') AS details_fragment, JSON_QUERY(jt.attributes, '$.labels') AS labels_fragment, JSON_TYPE(JSON_QUERY(jt.attributes, '$.details')) AS details_type FROM JSON_TABLE('[{"id":11,"attributes":{"details":{"tier":"gold"},"labels":["new","sale"]}},{"id":12,"attributes":{"labels":["clearance"]}}]', '$[*]' COLUMNS (item_id INT PATH '$.id', attributes JSON PATH '$.attributes')) AS jt ORDER BY jt.item_id
